Explains any GitHub repository in simple words, in your language. No AI, no account, free and open source.
1. Open a repository in the GitHub app.
2. Tap Share (the ⋮ menu or the share icon).

Translation happens on your phone. Download the English, Chinese, Japanese, Korean and Russian packs once (about 30 MB each, Wi-Fi recommended). Otherwise they download the first time they\'re needed.
⚠️ %1$d/%2$d downloaded. The others will be translated over the internet.

Shows a bubble on the right while the GitHub app is open. Tapping it opens the README of the repository on screen, translated into your language. It reads the screen only to find the repository name and does nothing in other apps.

Turn this on once: while you are inside a repository in the GitHub app, a 📖 bubble appears on the right. Tap it and the README opens in your language. Hold it to see which repository it found; drag it to move.
⚪ Bubble is off — under Accessibility → Downloaded apps, turn on GitTranslate.

If App info says \"App restricted\" or the bubble is greyed out: open App info below and confirm \"Remove restriction\" (on some phones: ⋮ at the top right → \"Allow restricted settings\"). Android asks this for every app installed outside the Play Store that uses accessibility.
GitHub\'s hourly limit is used up, so only the README is shown. Details come back later.
